     in a data/ folder next to this file, then render or run it chunk by chunk. -->

## Demo 1 — From values to a data frame

**Step 1. A vector is a column**

```{r}
#| label: d1-vector
# Five players' deaths, typed in by hand. c() combines values into a vector.
deaths <- c(2, 0, 5, 3, 1)

deaths          # print it
length(deaths)  # how many players
deaths[3]       # the third player: square brackets pick by position
deaths > 2      # a condition gives one TRUE/FALSE per player
sum(deaths > 2) # TRUE counts as 1, so this is a count, not a total
```

**Step 2. A missing value poisons the arithmetic**

```{r}
#| label: d1-na
# The fourth player's log was lost. NA means "not recorded", not zero.
deaths <- c(2, 0, 5, NA, 1)

mean(deaths)               # NA: R will not guess
mean(deaths, na.rm = TRUE) # say out loud what you are leaving out
```

**Step 3. Read the real file**

```{r}
#| label: d1-read
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# The path is relative to the project folder.
sessions <- read_csv("data/tidebreak_sessions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

**Step 4. Look before you touch**

```{r}
#| label: d1-look
glimpse(sessions)            # every column: name, type, first values
sessions |> count(cohort)    # the pipe reads "and then": take sessions, count cohorts
mean(sessions$deaths)        # $ pulls out one column as a vector
```

## Demo 2 — Describing, then looking

**Step 5. Centre and spread**

```{r}
#| label: d2-centre
kills <- sessions$kills

mean(kills)
median(kills)
sd(kills)                     # typical distance from the mean
IQR(kills)                    # width of the middle half
quantile(kills, c(0.1, 0.9))  # any percentiles you ask for
```

**Step 6. The shape, the groups, the counts**

```{r}
#| label: d2-plots
#| fig-alt:
#|   - "Histogram of seconds alive per session, from 60 to 180, with the tallest bar at 170 to 180 seconds."
#|   - "Boxplots of session length by build. Build A's box is lower and wider than Build B's."
#|   - "Bar chart of how sessions ended. Completed test is by far the most common, followed by frustrated and lost interest."
hist(sessions$time_alive_s, breaks = 15,
     main = "Seconds alive", xlab = "Seconds", col = "grey85")

boxplot(session_minutes ~ build, data = sessions,
        main = "Session length by build", ylab = "Minutes", col = "grey85")

quits <- sessions |> count(quit_reason, sort = TRUE)
barplot(quits$n, names.arg = quits$quit_reason,
        main = "How sessions ended", col = "grey85")
```

**Step 7. One summary per group**

```{r}
#| label: d2-groups
# group_by() splits the table; summarise() runs each summary once per piece.
sessions |>
  group_by(build) |>
  summarise(n          = n(),               # always say how many
            median_min = median(session_minutes),
            frustrated = mean(quit_reason == "Frustrated"))  # a proportion
```

**Step 8. Three shapes, and what the mean does to each**

```{r}
#| label: d2-shapes
#| fig-alt: "Three histograms side by side, each with a solid red mean line and a dashed median line. Awareness is roughly symmetric and the two lines almost coincide. Session length piles up near 32 minutes and its mean sits left of the median. Sentinel score has a separate low group, and its mean sits well left of the median."
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
shape <- function(x, title) {
  hist(x, breaks = 12, main = title, xlab = "", col = "grey85", border = "white")
  abline(v = mean(x), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2)       # mean: solid red
  abline(v = median(x), lty = 2, lwd = 2)               # median: dashed
}
shape(sessions$awareness, "Awareness")
shape(sessions$session_minutes, "Session minutes")
shape(sessions$score[sessions$archetype == "Sentinel"], "Sentinel score")
par(op)
```

**Step 9. The frame-rate trap**

```{r}
#| label: d2-frames
frames <- read_csv("data/tidebreak_frame_times.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Every summary per build in one table. p99: the frame time 99% of frames beat.
frames |>
  group_by(build) |>
  summarise(fps    = 1000 / mean(ms),
            median = median(ms),
            p99    = quantile(ms, 0.99))
```
